newsitem.title: ITALY: MOTOR RACING-FERRARI REACH ENGINE DEAL WITH SAUBER.
newsitem.headline: MOTOR RACING-FERRARI REACH ENGINE DEAL WITH SAUBER.

text.p: Ferrari announced on Friday they had agreed a two-year deal to provide engines for the Swiss Sauber Formula One team.

Ferrari said in a statement that under the agreement, reportedly killed off earlier in the month, the Italian company would set up an "ad-hoc autonomous structure" separate from its own Formula One team to work with Sauber.
It would produce engines to be used by Sauber in the 1997 and 1998 Formula One world championship.
The Italian team said earlier in the month they had pulled out of the deal because the Swiss group had been premature in announcing the agreement.
Sauber had announced they had reached a deal under which Ferrari would "manufacture, supply and develop" a Formula One engine for their use in 1997 and 1998.
